facts.value: keeps the draper's shop in Fore Street
facts.quote: I keep the draper's shop in Fore Street

facts.detail: under a loose board behind the counter
facts.quote: My cash-box lives under a loose board behind the counter

facts.value: writes to her sister Jane where the cash-box is hidden
facts.quote: I wrote to my sister Jane and told her where it was

facts.value: told by Ann Tolley to nobody but her sister Jane
facts.quote: I have never told anyone else

facts.detail: at her aunt's funeral, the shop shut
facts.quote: went with Jane to our aunt's funeral at St. Mary's

facts.detail: beside Ann Tolley the whole hour
facts.quote: She was beside me the whole hour
the board was up, and the cash-box was gone

facts.value: nothing else touched: the till and its two pounds of silver as Ann Tolley left them
facts.quote: Nothing else in the shop had been touched

facts.value: Ann Tolley's errand boy, in and out of the shop all week
facts.quote: Dick, my errand boy, is in and out of the shop all week

facts.detail: on the round, two miles off, by the delivery book: names signed at three houses there
facts.quote: my delivery book has him on the round to Hilltop, two miles off, from one o'clock until four

facts.value: reads Ann Tolley's letter aloud at her breakfast table, not thinking what was in it
facts.quote: she read it aloud at her breakfast table, not thinking what was in it

facts.detail: at her breakfast table, her lodger
facts.quote: Her lodger, Mr. Voss, was at the table

facts.detail: he heard the letter read aloud
facts.quote: Her lodger, Mr. Voss, was at the table

facts.value: finds the cash-box in Mr. Voss's trunk, its lock broken open
facts.quote: The constable found my cash-box in Mr. Voss's trunk
